correctness.rationale: Under the skew color-change rule any vertex with one white neighbor may force. Nonempty terminal white sets are precisely skew forts, in which no vertex has exactly one neighbor. In a clique bouquet, a minimal fort is either three peripheral vertices within one blade, or the white hub plus two vertices in every blade; all other white configurations contain a smaller one of these. Their avoidance forces at most two whites per blade and either a blue hub or one blade with at most one white. This establishes (1+z)prod(Q_i)-prod(E_i) and shows all inclusion-minimal forcing sets have size N-2r, counted by prod C(n_i,2)+sum_j n_j prod_{i ne j} C(n_i,2). A triple fort bounds maximum failing cardinality at N-3 when any blade size>=3, hence span 2r-2; all two-vertex blades instead have only the all-white fort, span zero. Independent adjacency/saturation simulation exhaustively checked six small heterogeneous blade profiles and their forcing histograms, rather than merely trusting the supplied 182-profile log. The proof explicitly requires r>=2 and every n_i>=2; singleton blades and standard (blue-only) forcing are not included.
